expectation: Membrane/granular ring on neutrophils (and some eosinophils): scattered single round cells with lobed nuclei, sparse in lamina propria and vessels, denser in inflamed foci, crypt abscesses or surface exudate; epithelium and muscle negative.
observed: A: haze over the whole tissue, glow along the top edges, radial fibre streaks in the right muscle, and round debris blobs inside and outside the tissue. B/C: diffuse haze and blobs; crypts negative. D: a cluster of granular ring-stained cells at the edge. E: a few granular foci; CD11b shows no structure.
why: A few granular ring-like cells fit neutrophils, but most of the signal is haze, edge glow, fibre streaks and debris, and the partner can't confirm them.
notes: Most CD66b signal is haze, edge glow and debris. A small edge cluster (D) and a few lamina propria foci look like granulocytes, though eosinophil autofluorescence can't be excluded. CD11b has no cellular structure, so row E doesn't help.
